sentences.text: John Adams -LRB- October 30 -LSB- O.S. October 19 -RSB- 1735 -- July 4 , 1826 -RRB- was an American patriot who served as the second President of the United States -LRB- 1797 -- 1801 -RRB- and the first Vice President -LRB- 1789 -- 97 -RRB- .	American patriot	Patriot (American Revolution)	second President of the United States	List of Presidents of the United States	Vice President	Vice President of the United States

He was a lawyer , diplomat , statesman , political theorist , and , as a Founding Father , a leader of the movement for American independence from Great Britain .	Founding Father	Founding Fathers of the United States	Great Britain	Kingdom of Great Britain
He was also a dedicated diarist and correspondent , particularly with his wife and closest advisor Abigail .	Abigail	Abigail Adams

He collaborated with his cousin , revolutionary leader Samuel Adams , but he established his own prominence prior to the American Revolution .	Samuel Adams	Samuel Adams	American Revolution	American Revolution

After the Boston Massacre , he provided a successful -LRB- though unpopular -RRB- legal defense of the accused British soldiers , in the face of severe local anti-British sentiment and driven by his devotion to the right to counsel and the `` protect -LSB- ion -RSB- of innocence '' .	Boston Massacre	Boston Massacre	right to counsel	right to counsel

Adams was a delegate from Massachusetts to the Continental Congress , where he played a leading role in persuading Congress to declare independence .	Massachusetts	Province of Massachusetts Bay	Continental Congress	Continental Congress

He assisted Thomas Jefferson in drafting the Declaration of Independence in 1776 , and was its foremost advocate in the Congress .	Thomas Jefferson	Thomas Jefferson	Thomas	Thomas Boylston Adams (1772–1832)	Declaration of Independence	United States Declaration of Independence

As a diplomat in Europe , he helped negotiate the eventual peace treaty with Great Britain , and acquired vital governmental loans from Amsterdam bankers .	Great Britain	Kingdom of Great Britain	peace treaty	Treaty of Paris (1783)	Amsterdam	Amsterdam

Adams was the primary author of the Massachusetts Constitution in 1780 which influenced American political theory , as did his earlier Thoughts on Government -LRB- 1776 -RRB- .	Massachusetts	Province of Massachusetts Bay	Massachusetts Constitution	Massachusetts Constitution	Thoughts on Government	Thoughts on Government

Adams 's credentials as a revolutionary secured for him two terms as President George Washington 's vice president -LRB- 1789 to 1797 -RRB- and also his own election in 1796 as the second president .	George Washington	George Washington

In his single term as president , he encountered fierce criticism from the Jeffersonian Republicans , as well as the dominant faction in his own Federalist Party , led by his rival Alexander Hamilton .	Federalist	Federalist Party	Jeffersonian Republicans	Democratic-Republican Party	Federalist Party	Federalist Party	Alexander Hamilton	Alexander Hamilton

Adams signed the controversial Alien and Sedition Acts , and built up the army and navy in the face of an undeclared naval `` Quasi-War '' with France .	Alien and Sedition Acts	Alien and Sedition Acts	Quasi-War	Quasi-War
The major accomplishment of his presidency was a peaceful resolution of the conflict in the face of Hamilton 's opposition .
Due to his strong posture on defense , Adams is `` often called the father of the American Navy '' .	American Navy	American Navy
He was the first U.S. president to reside in the executive mansion , now known as the White House .	White House	White House

In 1800 , Adams lost re-election to Thomas Jefferson and retired to Massachusetts .	Thomas Jefferson	Thomas Jefferson	Massachusetts	Province of Massachusetts Bay	Thomas	Thomas Boylston Adams (1772–1832)	1800	United States presidential election, 1800
He eventually resumed his friendship with Jefferson upon the latter 's own retirement by initiating a correspondence which lasted fourteen years .
He and his wife established a family of politicians , diplomats , and historians now referred to as the Adams political family .	Adams political family	Adams political family
Adams was the father of John Quincy Adams , the sixth President of the United States .	John Quincy	John Quincy Adams	John Quincy Adams	John Quincy Adams	sixth	List of Presidents of the United States
He died on the fiftieth anniversary of the adoption of the Declaration of Independence , and the same day as Jefferson .	Declaration of Independence	United States Declaration of Independence
